The Godot SDK's UI kit, in GDScript, for desktop, phones, tablets, the Steam Deck and TVs. One call
gates a game and runs every screen the license needs: the boot, Activate with the key field, the
sign-in form, offline activation, Replace a device, the blocking states with their fixes, offline
grace, the update prompt and the settings. Every screen is also a scene of its own, and each one
reads a headless controller that a game's own menus can read too. The rest of the Godot SDK is on
the [Godot](/docs/build/sdks/godot/) page; to draw your own screens instead, see
[Your own UI](/docs/build/sdks/godot/your-own-ui/).

<KitFacts kit="godot" />

The kit has three layers, and a game can stop at any of them:

| Layer                       | What you write                        | Where                       |
| --------------------------- | ------------------------------------- | --------------------------- |
| Drop-in                     | `await PolarisKey.boot()`             | [Below](#the-one-line-flow) |
| Scenes                      | Place a scene, or let it find the SDK | [Scenes](#scenes)           |
| Controllers and view models | Draw every control yourself           | [Headless](#headless)       |

## Install

The kit is part of the addon at `res://addons/polaris_key/`, installed from Polaris Key's Godot
feed ([Installing the SDKs from the feeds](/docs/build/install/)). It runs on Godot 4.4
and later, and bundles Rubik and JetBrains Mono (both OFL).

## The one-line flow

```gdscript
extends Node


func _ready() -> void:
	await PolarisKey.boot()
	get_tree().change_scene_to_file("res://game/title.tscn")
```

`boot()` reads `res://polaris_key.tres`, syncs, gates on the license and checks for an update on
the `PKeyBoot` screen, and returns once the player is through. A stop keeps its card on screen
with Try again, and the await waits through the retries. The settings open over the game in one
line too, and close with Close, Escape or a pad's B:

```gdscript
func open_settings() -> void:
	PKeySettingsPanel.open(self)
```

## Scenes

Each screen is a scene under `addons/polaris_key/ui/`, with a view script and a headless
controller. The class is the name to use in code; the gate's scene file is `pkey_gate.tscn` and
its class is `PKeyGateView`.

| Class                  | Scene                                     | Shows                                                                                  |
| ---------------------- | ----------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `PKeyBoot`             | `boot/pkey_boot.tscn`                     | The stages from start to ready, and a card with Try again on a stop                    |
| `PKeyGateView`         | `gate/pkey_gate.tscn`                     | The license gate: activation, grace, expired, blocked                                  |
| `PKeyActivationPanel`  | `activation/pkey_activation_panel.tscn`   | Key entry, sign-in, free tier, offline activation, Replace a device                    |
| `PKeySignInDialog`     | `sign_in/pkey_sign_in_dialog.tscn`        | The device code, its QR code and the countdown                                         |
| `PKeyOfflineDialog`    | `offline/pkey_offline_dialog.tscn`        | The request code, and the import of an activation file                                 |
| `PKeyUpdatePrompt`     | `update/pkey_update_prompt.tscn`          | An update offer, with the action the install's outlet allows                           |
| `PKeyStatusBanner`     | `banner/pkey_status_banner.tscn`          | Offline grace, an expired check, an available update                                   |
| `PKeySettingsPanel`    | `settings/pkey_settings_panel.tscn`       | The product's settings, with a lock on each managed value                              |
| `PKeyDeviceList`       | `devices/pkey_device_list.tscn`           | The devices using the license, with Rename and Remove in place                         |
| `PKeyLicenseChoice`    | `license_choice/pkey_license_choice.tscn` | Which license this device uses, when an account holds several                          |
| `PKeyAccountTab`       | `settings/pkey_account_tab.tscn`          | The Account and license pane, embedded in settings or opened as a page                 |
| `PKeyToast`            | `toast/pkey_toast.tscn`                   | A brief message over the game, with at most two actions                                |
| `PKeyUpdateProgress`   | `progress/pkey_update_progress.tscn`      | Download and install progress for an update or content packs                           |
| `PKeyPaywall`          | `paywall/pkey_paywall.tscn`               | An upsell for a tier: Upgrade (store) or Buy in your browser, Redeem, Restore          |
| `PKeyDeviceLimit`      | `device_limit/pkey_device_limit.tscn`     | "Your license is on 3 of 3 devices": replace the least recent, or open the manage page |
| `PKeyEntitlementBadge` | `badge/pkey_entitlement_badge.tscn`       | "Included with" chips for the user-facing entitlements the license holds               |

A scene finds the `PolarisKey` autoload by itself and follows its `state_changed` signal. To place
one in your own layout, instance it and add it as a child:

```gdscript
extends Control

const GateScene := preload("res://addons/polaris_key/ui/gate/pkey_gate.tscn")


func _ready() -> void:
	var gate: PKeyGateView = GateScene.instantiate()
	gate.usable.connect(_on_usable)
	add_child(gate)


func _on_usable() -> void:
	print("the license lets the game run")
```

A scene lays itself out for its window: two panes on a wide landscape panel, one column at 4:3,
and on a phone the page full-bleed with the product at the top and the actions docked at the
bottom, the primary on top. A scene a game's own menu holds draws no card of its own. Every
interactive control is in one wrapping focus chain, so `ui_up`, `ui_down`, `ui_accept` and
`ui_cancel` operate every screen on a keyboard, a gamepad or a TV remote.

## Headless

Each scene reads a controller, and a game that draws its own screens can read the same ones. They
are in `addons/polaris_key/ui/` and are pure functions of the state they are given:

| Class                         | Answers                                                                        |
| ----------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `PKeyGateController`          | Which screen a license status renders, with its copy keys and its controls     |
| `PKeyActivationController`    | Which ways to activate this build offers, and the copy key for each refusal    |
| `PKeySignInController`        | The copy key for how a sign-in ended, the countdown and the identity line      |
| `PKeyUpdatePromptController`  | Whether an update answer shows, its copy keys, its action and whether it locks |
| `PKeyDevicesController`       | The roster as rows, how long ago each device was last used, which is this one  |
| `PKeyLicenseChoiceController` | The rows the license step offers, the selected one and what each says          |
| `PKeyAccountController`       | What the Account and license pane knows: tier, holder, seats, update rows      |
| `PKeyToastController`         | A toast's model view, its status glyph and its actions                         |
| `PKeyProgressController`      | The model input for a download, the time left and the sizes as one unit        |

[Your own UI](/docs/build/sdks/godot/your-own-ui/#gate-status-screen-and-copy-key) maps every status
to its screen and copy keys.

The view models in `addons/polaris_key/ui/model/` are the port of the shared headless layer. Each
is a pure function of one input Dictionary and answers the state, the catalog copy keys, the
actions and the design decisions (the one primary, what takes focus, which links and QR codes may
show):

```gdscript
const Models := preload("res://addons/polaris_key/ui/model/models.gd")


func headless_view() -> void:
	var view := Models.view_of("PolarisKeyGate", {"gate": {"status": "revoked"}})
	print(view["state"])  # blocked
```

`sign_in_session.gd` is the sign-in form's state machine over the SDK's sign-in primitives, and
`copy_format.gd` formats a catalog copy key in the player's locale. The shipped scenes read the
controllers above; the view models run the shared UI state matrix, so a screen fed the same inputs
shows the same step with the same copy key in every SDK.

## Theming

The Polaris Key look is the default, dark, in the product's accent; `ui_branding = "none"`
follows the game's own theme. The options are on `PKeyOptions` (`ui_brand_scheme`, `ui_accent`,
`ui_theme`, `ui_density`, `ui_product_name`, `ui_product_icon`); the fields are on
[Theming](/docs/build/ui/theming/). `ui_reduce_motion` and `ui_reduce_transparency` follow the
system's settings by default (`auto`, from Godot 4.5) and can be forced `on` or `off`.

## Game look

A dialog over your game (sign in, the update prompt, settings, offline activation) is glass on a dimmed frame: its card is nearly opaque (94 % dark, 96 % light) until the blur ships, and the scrim is 42 % dark and 35 % light. It is fully opaque on a phone's docked sheet, under `ui_reduce_transparency`, on the web and under the `gl_compatibility` renderer. A dialog fades in from 98 % scale and a pressed button settles to 98 %; neither moves under `ui_reduce_motion`, and neither depends on `Engine.time_scale`. The focus ring has a glow.

| Option                         | Does                                                                                                                                                                       |
| ------------------------------ | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `ui_brand_scheme = "system"`   | Follows the OS: re-checked when the game regains focus and when a dialog opens, dark where the OS has no preference. The kit never takes your system-theme callback.       |
| `ui_sound_hook`                | A Callable taking one event. The kit plays no sound itself.                                                                                                                |
| `PolarisKey.ui_sound` (signal) | The same events, and it survives `configure()`. Use it when the options cannot carry a Callable.                                                                           |
| `ui_haptics`                   | Off by default. A short vibration on a handheld (Android needs the `VIBRATE` permission) and a weak rumble on the pad last used, for confirm, back, error, open and close. |

The events are `open` and `close` (a dialog; `open` alone, with no focus sound), `focus` (moved by the keyboard or a pad, never by a mouse click), `confirm` (a button that acts), `back` (Cancel, Later, Close, Dismiss, Escape or the pad's back button) and `error` (a refusal shown).

`PKeyInputGlyphs` draws the confirm or back control of the last input device: the keyboard key bound to `ui_accept` or `ui_cancel`, and on a pad the button bound to it (A and B on an Xbox pad, a cross and a circle on a PlayStation pad, B and A on a Nintendo pad). A game that remaps those actions is followed. `PKeyHintBar` pairs each glyph with a bare verb from the catalog in the running locale ("Select", "Activate", the screen's own Cancel or Later, or Back): one footer at the bottom right of the title-safe area, outside the panel, on every screen that offers a choice; on a phone, or where a card fills the screen, it is the last row of the panel. It shows for a keyboard or a pad (a mouse that moves counts as the keyboard), never for touch.

## Powered by Polaris Locker

`ui_powered_by = true` adds the Locker line (the micro mark at 16 px and the phrase) as the last item in the settings scroll; never the gate or boot. `ui_powered_by_style` is `"line"` by default. On a credits or about scene you place, a `PKeyPoweredBy` node with `allow_badge = true` draws the 320 × 104 badge with `"badge"` where 320 px are free, else the line.

## Localization

Every string the scenes show is a key of `PKeyUiCopy`, in English, passed through `tr()`: translate
the English defaults with an ordinary Translation, or rename a string with
`PKeyUiCopy.overrides`, without forking a scene. The generated gettext tables in
`addons/polaris_key/ui/locale/` are keyed on the shared catalog ids and only the view models'
`copy_format.gd` reads them: the scenes do not load them, so those `.po` files do not translate a
scene yet.
